headline: High: pdf.js can ingest PDFs while the paired content-writing agent has broad egress, creating default-path leakage and cascading misuse risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct prompt injection is not established. However, agent_b reads PDF files and agent_a has broad network egress, so if outputs are manually bridged or copied into a shared workspace, PDF content could be treated as instructions. This is weaker than medium because no default shared filesystem or parser bridge is shown.
conditions: IF the operator copies pdf.js output into agent_a prompts or a shared file
IF both agents are pointed at the same writable workspace
mitigations: Keep agents in separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste bridging between outputs and prompts
Use a human review step before reusing PDF-derived text
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to transferred content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent_b processes PDF documents and agent_a has broad network egress, so a default workflow can move document content from B into A and then off-host. The pair does not show shared credentials or a shared filesystem, but the combination still creates a plausible leakage path for sensitive PDFs in ordinary use.
conditions: IF PDF documents handled by agent_b contain sensitive data
IF agent_a receives any extracted text or summaries from agent_b
mitigations: Do not pass sensitive PDFs from B to A
Restrict agent_a egress to allowlisted destinations
Use redaction before any handoff
Log and review all outbound requests
requires-engineering: isolate the agents at the network boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: The profiles show overlapping file-oriented workflows only indirectly: agent_b can handle PDF files and supports multiple instances, while agent_a has no write surface or concurrency details. There is no evidence of shared mutable writes, git state, or overlapping OAuth scopes, so conflict risk is limited and uncertain.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same directory
IF an external orchestrator gives them shared mutable state
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Serialize any shared writes
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent_b can process PDFs and browser-based tests, so it may consume text produced by agent_a; if that text is treated as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream document handling. Agent_a is a content-writing agent, which increases the chance that B ingests generated prose without verification. No direct action authority is shown, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a's generated text as source material
IF no verification step checks extracted facts before reuse
mitigations: Require source citations for any reused text
Add a verification pass before B acts on A's output
Mark generated content as untrusted
Limit B to read-only transformations
requires-engineering: enforce provenance checks in the pipeline

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, and agent_b only touches PDF documents while agent_a's data classes are empty. Compliance risk is therefore limited to unspecified deployment choices, not a proven pairwise violation. The other agent is not cited beyond the pair context because no specific compliance surface is exposed.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into pdf.js workflows
IF deployment policy requires residency or retention controls not configured here
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Document retention settings
Review deployment residency before use
requires-engineering: add compliance controls to the orchestrator
